minutes.headline: Select Board declared a local COVID-19 state of emergency 4-0 with one abstention, and set Town Meeting for June 13.
minutes.summary: First fully remote Select Board meeting, held by Zoom with roll-call votes. The board got the town manager's COVID-19 update, declared a local state of emergency, and adopted a revised budget calendar ending in a June 13 Town Meeting. It also designated a member to sign warrants, granted a restaurant closure, released executive session minutes, and heard counsel on the dangerous dog appeal.

public_comment.topic: Finance Committee plans to meet next Thursday to review the budget information and schedule, and asked for the schedule to be sent.
Promoted the United Way of North Central Mass COVID-19 fund and the club's virtual programming for kids.

budget_items.what_was_said: A member asked about benefits of the declaration; the emergency allows spending and transfers within the budget if the emergency management line goes over.
Counsel and the town manager said a local declaration may speed federal aid review. Departments are tracking COVID-related expenses, including volunteer hours.
The town manager said the budget must be rebuilt from scratch, including forecasting, given the new financial situation.
The town manager said the state confirmed remaining FY20 local aid payments will come; Chapter 70 and local aid for next year are not yet known.
The town manager imposed a spending and hiring freeze for the rest of the fiscal year except essential and public safety items.
The town manager recommended limiting the design firm's scope given fiscal uncertainty.
A competitive bid came back from Blue Cross Blue Shield, to be reviewed by the public employee committee.
The agency confirmed the earmark will be released in full once the contract is signed.
The board signed bond anticipation notes for the Saliba property and ladder truck borrowing.

decisions.decision: Caucus to be rescheduled once the town clerk recommends an annual election date.
Board will lobby the town clerk to hold the town election after Town Meeting; the election date is left to the clerk and the board.
Town manager to bring a proposed evaluation timeline to the next meeting.
Another remote meeting planned for March 31.
Board will wait for the appeal before seeking confinement of the dogs, pursuing it when the courts return to normal.

what_happened.line: The Select Board declared a local state of emergency for COVID-19, 4-0 with one abstention, at its first fully remote meeting.
The board adopted a revised budget calendar that ends with annual Town Meeting on June 13, 2020.
The town manager said the FY21 budget must be rebuilt from scratch and announced a spending and hiring freeze for the rest of FY20, except essential and public safety items.
The board named the chair to sign warrants for as long as the emergency lasts, and approved the temporary closure of Sean Patrick's restaurant.
The town manager said remaining FY20 state local aid will be paid, but Chapter 70 and local aid for next year are not yet known.

why_it_matters: The FY21 budget that residents will vote on at Town Meeting is being rebuilt, and state aid for next year is unknown, so the tax rate and local services for FY21 are uncertain.

The emergency declaration lets the town spend and transfer within the budget if the emergency management line runs over, and may speed federal reimbursement review, which bears on how much of the cost falls on local taxes.
watch_next: Finance Committee meeting next Thursday to review the budget information and schedule.
Another remote Select Board meeting planned for March 31, with the town manager's proposed evaluation timeline due.
